text.p: Specialty chemicals group Laporte Plc on Monday reported a 12 percent rise in pre-tax profit before exceptional items to 127.0 million pounds ($219.2 million), coming in above market expectations.
The results increase comes after Laporte simplified its group structure and closed or sold about 34 percent of its operating units in 1996 to boost its performance.

The headline figures were hit by exceptional charges of 48.3 million pounds. This is the second year that results have been affected by hefty charges, reflecting the efforts of Laporte's new management team to reshape the business to focus on more profitable specialty chemicals and performance materials.

Laporte, which was forced to issue a shock profits warning in November 1995, said benefits of the restructuring were feeding through, with operating profit margins improving to 12.9 percent of sales from 11.8 percent a year earlier.
A series of disposals, including December's 110 million pound sale of the European adhesives operations, had helped clear the group's debt during the year, Laporte said.
However it warned that "a strong pound and competitive market conditions will together make for a challenging backcloth for the current year." --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
